values.value: Of the things wired into HubSpot — app-marketplace integrations, forms and CTAs embedded on sites you do not control, webhooks, Operations Hub custom code, ad-audience syncs — how many are owned by a team outside marketing, and how many would have to be re-pointed by someone else before you could switch off HubSpot?

[{"value":1,"label":"Several are owned outside marketing, including forms or CTAs embedded on sites another team controls, and nobody has a full list of who owns what."},{"value":2,"label":"The main ones are known and at least one sits with another team, so cutover depends on a schedule marketing does not set."},{"value":3,"label":"A small number of integrations, all with a named owner inside or beside marketing, and any embedded forms are on pages we control."},{"value":4,"label":"Nothing outside marketing depends on HubSpot. Forms are on our own pages and the integrations we have could be re-pointed by this team alone."}]

Ask for the installed-apps list, the connected ad accounts, and the count of forms embedded outside their own domain. The last one is the number they will not have. Then ask, per item, who would have to do the work — the answer that matters is the owner, not the count, which Integration Surface already collects.
Worth knowing before you answer: which teams own the integrations connected to HubSpot, and whether any of your forms or CTAs are embedded on pages another team looks after.

migration-accelerator/capabilities/platforms/hubspot.yaml — forms_and_ctas_rebuild, "Major for both, and largely target-independent — the hard part is the customer's web estate, not the target platform", and operations_hub_custom_code and ads_audience_sync, all three of which are things wired INTO the platform by somebody else. skills/mce-mcn-helper/references/skills/10-roadmap.md — the external-dependency and risk-register framing, where integrations owned outside marketing set the roadmap's outer bound, which is the anchor this scale is now built on. RECALIBRATED FROM LAYER 1, and the reason is the second axis rather than the manifest. The base anchors counted integrations ("many external systems", "several known", "a handful", "one or two"), and migration-accelerator/instrument/migration-accelerator/complexity.yaml's integration_surface dimension counts them too — so a respondent met the same question twice, six screens apart, and could reasonably conclude the form was not paying attention. The two axes are genuinely different and the questions now say so: complexity asks HOW MANY are wired in, readiness asks WHO OWNS THEM and whether cutover waits on somebody else. That is the blast-radius risk the slot's theme names, it is not a size measure, and it is the answer that sets the roadmap's outer bound. The named examples are unchanged; only the scale moved.
